contexts.text: The phantasy of the learned concerning what is immaterial... from which no other conception can be had, than that, being immaterial, it is either so obscure that it cannot be apprehended by any idea, or that it is nothing; for what is immaterial involves such [an idea]; when yet it is exactly the contrary.
As there are few who have any other idea about Angels and Spirits than as of what is immaterial; and thence that they are only thoughts...
